title: Storm brewing in Bay to bring heavy rain to south Bengal's coast from 19 November
dek: The IMD expects heavy rain in South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur and thunderstorms in Kolkata later this week, and has told fishermen to stay out of the northern Bay on 19 and 20 November. The storm itself is forecast to head for Andhra Pradesh.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
South Bengal's coastal districts are likely to get heavy rain from Thursday, 19 November, as a storm now forming in the south Bay of Bengal moves north, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said. The system is expected to become a cyclonic storm, likely to be named Akvan, by Monday evening, and to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday. Its centre is forecast to head for the Andhra Pradesh coast, hundreds of kilometres south-west of Bengal, but its outer bands are expected to bring rain and gusty winds to the state.

In its 2.30 am national bulletin on Monday, the IMD forecast light to moderate rain at many places in Gangetic West Bengal on 19 and 20 November, with heavy rain at isolated places. It has told fishermen not to venture into the northwest Bay of Bengal, the waters off the Bengal and Odisha coasts, on 19 and 20 November.

## District by district

The IMD's district forecasts for Bengal, as reported on Sunday, point to heavy rain in the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from 19 to 21 November, and downpours in Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on 20 and 21 November. Thunderstorms with winds of up to 40 kmph are likely in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal, the reports said. The dates in the district forecast run a day longer than those in the national bulletin; the IMD's later bulletins will settle the timing.

The IMD's national bulletin forecasts squally winds of 45-55 kmph gusting to 65 kmph over the northwest Bay of Bengal from the night of 18 November, rising to 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph from the morning of 19 November until the morning of 20 November, with rough to very rough seas on 19 November. Those conditions matter for the trawler fleets of Digha, Kakdwip, Namkhana and Frasergunj, which work these waters.

## A brief end to the chill

The weather system is also expected to push temperatures up. Darjeeling was the coldest place in Bengal on Sunday at 8.2°C, and Kolkata's minimum was 21.3°C, according to reports. Day and night temperatures across south Bengal are expected to rise by 2-3°C from 18 November as moist winds from the Bay arrive, the reports said, citing the weather office.

## Why it matters for Bengal

Rain in the second half of November comes as the aman paddy crop, south Bengal's main rice crop, approaches harvest, and as potato planting begins in districts such as Hooghly and Paschim Medinipur; heavy rain at this stage can flatten ripe paddy and waterlog fields. Bengal escaped the worst of Cyclone Arnab and Cyclone Murasu, which hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha in late October and early November.

## What happens next

The IMD said its next national bulletin would be issued at 9 am on Monday. The Regional Meteorological Centre in Kolkata, which received Monday's bulletin, issues the district-level warnings for Bengal. The state government has not yet announced any special measures for the storm. The Declaration will update this story as forecasts for Bengal are revised.
